key: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
s: The verse opens a hymn of origins ending with the Creator forming sun, moon, heaven and earth; Sāyaṇa, on 10.190.1, takes ‘Law’ as true intention and ‘Truth’ as true speech, born of fervour spent for creation, which he explains as contemplating what would be made.

evidence.words: ऋतमिति सत्यनाम । ऋतं मानसं यथार्थसंकल्पनं सत्यं वाचिकं यथार्थभाषणम् । … तत्सर्वमभीद्धादभितप्ताद्ब्रह्मणा पुरा सृष्ट्यर्थं कृतात्तपसोऽधि । अध्युपर्यर्थे । उपर्यजायत । उदपद्यत । … तपश्चात्र स्रष्टव्यपर्यालोचनलक्षणम् ।
evidence.gloss: Ṛta is a name for truth: ṛta is of the mind, a true intention; satya is of speech, a true statement … All this arose upon the kindled tapas performed of old by brahmaṇā (instrumental; he does not say whether the god Brahmā or brahman) for the sake of creation; adhi means ‘upon’; it was born, arose … Tapas here has the character of contemplating what is to be created.

reason: The problem holds: the opening clause had no subject and read as if Sāyaṇa opened the hymn, and the closing participle had none either. Re-opened packet.js veda 126 --verse 10.190.1. The plain sense now has its own subject (‘The verse opens a hymn of origins...’; 10.190.3 has Dhatar forming Sun, Moon, Heaven, Earth), and the closing clause is tied to the fervour by ‘which he explains as’, carried by तपश्चात्र स्रष्टव्यपर्यालोचनलक्षणम्. Unlike the critic’s fix, it keeps the refuter’s correction: ‘for creation’ (सृष्ट्यर्थं), not ‘before creation’, which is Wilson’s note and not Sāyaṇa’s words, and no named agent. ‘Three-verse’ and ‘of old’ were cut to stay within 45 words. verse.js ok (10.190.1, at [1026,1]); entry-check ok.
